/// SGS on 1 000 000 lattice nodes: 16 realizations along a shared path
/// against one along a random path.
fn shared(c: &mut Criterion) {
    let (data, values, _) = inputs();
    let geometry = ceres_core::Geometry { origin: [0.0; 3], size: [0.2, 0.2, 1.0], count: [1000, 1000, 1], rotation: [0.0; 3] };
    let lattice = simulation::Lattice::regular(geometry);
    let grid: Vec<_> = (0..lattice.len()).map(|m| lattice.location(m)).collect();
    let vg = Variogram::single(Model::Spherical, 1.0, 40.0);
    let search = vec![Search { min_samples: 1, max_samples: 24, radius: 60.0, ..Default::default() }];
    let mut group = c.benchmark_group("SGS, 1 000 000 nodes");
    group.sample_size(10);
    group.bench_function("shared path, 16 realizations", |b| {
        let shared = simulation::SharedSgs { lattice: &lattice, search: &search, levels: None, seed: 1 };
        b.iter(|| black_box(simulation::sgs_shared(&data, &values, None, None, None, None, &vg, &shared, 0..16, None).unwrap()))
    });
    group.bench_function("random path, 1 realization", |b| {
        let params = SgsParams { search: search.clone(), seed: 1 };
        b.iter(|| black_box(sgs(&data, &values, None, None, &grid, &vg, &params, None).unwrap()))
    });
    group.finish();
}

"""
# NN. SGS along a shared path

On a block model, SGS runs every realization along one multigrid path: coarse cells first, then finer ones. A node's
neighbors and kriging weights then depend on the path alone, so they are found once for a batch of realizations and
reused by all of them; only the noise differs. `path="random"` draws a new path per realization instead. Both
reproduce the histogram and the variogram; the shared path is several times faster on large grids.
"""

# %% [hidden]
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).parent if "__file__" in globals() else Path.cwd()
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE.parents[1]))

# %%
import ceres as cs
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from common import save

# %% [markdown]
# Walker Lake V, simulated as in topics 36 and 70, on a 1 m grid of 260 x 300 cells.

# %%
samples = cs.datasets.walker_lake()
xy, v = samples.coords, samples["V"]
weights = cs.cell_declustering(xy, v, sizes=np.arange(2.5, 102.5, 2.5)).weights
y = cs.NormalScore(tails=(0.0, v.max())).fit_transform(v, weights=weights)
azimuth, lag, max_lag = 170.0, 10.0, 120.0
major = cs.experimental_variogram(xy, y, lag, max_lag, azimuth=azimuth).fit("spherical")
minor = cs.experimental_variogram(xy, y, lag, max_lag, azimuth=azimuth + 90).fit("spherical")
total, a_major = major.sill, major.structures[0].range
gaussian = cs.Variogram(
    [("spherical", major.structures[0].sill / total, a_major)],
    nugget=major.nugget / total,
    rotation=(azimuth, 0, 0),
    ratios=(min(minor.structures[0].range / a_major, 1.0), 1.0),
)
grid = cs.BlockModel(origin=(0.5, 0.5), size=(1, 1), count=(260, 300))
sgs = cs.SGS(gaussian, cs.Search(radius=100, max_samples=24)).fit(samples, "V", weights=weights)

runs = {}
for path in ["shared", "random"]:
    start = time.perf_counter()
    runs[path] = sgs.simulate(grid, n=20, seed=42, realizations=True, path=path)
    print(f"{path:6} path: {time.perf_counter() - start:5.1f} s for 20 realizations of {len(grid.centroids):,} nodes")

# %% [markdown]
# Both paths reproduce the declustered histogram and the variogram model along N170°; the bands overlap.

# %%
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 3.8), layout="constrained")
for ax, (path, summary) in zip(axes, runs.items()):
    check = cs.check_realizations(grid, summary, samples, "V", weights=weights, variogram=gaussian, lag=lag, max_lag=max_lag)
    cs.plot.variogram_reproduction(check, ax=ax)
    ax.set(xlabel="Lag distance (m)", title=f"{path} path")
save(fig, "variograms")

docs.title: Self-review
docs.text:
• Spec coverage: shared default + random option (Tasks 7, 11); multigrid coarse-to-fine seeded (4); template + rank instead of growing tree (5, 6); weights once per batch, applied to all realizations (6, 7); RAM-sized batches, auto from free memory, overridable (10, 11); deterministic within-level parallelism via waves + counter noise (1, 7); domains/trend/passes/collocated (9); fallbacks named (9, 11); non-lattice targets fall back (11); histogram/variogram vs random, exact at data, threads and batch invariance (7, 8, 11); memory per node (design summary, 10); benchmark at 1M+ vs today (12); PRs ≤ ~400 lines (A–D).
  • The occupancy bitmap from the discussion is replaced by the u32 rank array: a node is a neighbor iff its rank is smaller, which is the precedence the bitmap would track, and it also marks datum nodes (u32::MAX).
  • Weights are recomputed per batch (path rebuilt per batch too; it is deterministic from the seed, so identical).

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
1. Multivariate SGS factors. MultivariateSimulation back-transforms all factors of a realization together over every node (transform.back(&rows) builds one Vec per node): at 1e9 nodes × 15 factors that is ~120 GB per realization in f64, before any path choice. Scaling it needs summaries fed by node chunks (an Accumulator that adds a slice of nodes), which plan 3 (turning bands, chunk-first) also needs. Proposal: keep multivariate on the random path here and add the shared path to it after plan 3 lands the chunked accumulator. Agree?
  2. Imputed heterotopic data (impute=) change data values, and so the normal-score transform, per realization. The plan's per-node constant folds data scores into one number; per-realization data would need data weights kept per node instead (+8 B per data neighbor per chunk only, cheap). Only matters once (1) is done.
  3. Default multigrid depth. default_levels uses half the template reach, at most 6. If Task 8's variogram check shows under-reproduction at short lags, should the default be shallower, or exposed as a levels= keyword in Python (currently Rust-only)?
  4. Quantiles at scale. quantiles= stores every value of every realization as f32 (4 × n B/node: 400 GB at 1e9 nodes × 100 realizations). Out of scope here; worth an approximate streaming quantile (or histogram per node) in a separate plan?
  5. Search features left on the random path (octant, high-grade, soft, local anisotropy, simulated domains): which of these do your 1e9-cell runs actually use? Each is a follow-up of its own (octant needs per-octant counting over the merged data+node list; local anisotropy needs per-node templates).
  6. Memory budget of 70 % of free memory — acceptable default, or would you rather have an explicit memory= keyword (GB) in place of or next to batch=?

docs.title: Decisions (2026-09-27)
docs.text:
• The shared path ships with the supported subset; octant, high-grade, soft boundaries, local anisotropy, simulated domains, points and sub-blocked targets keep falling back to path="random". Full coverage, and multivariate SGS on the shared path, wait for a later plan.
  • Memory: 70% of free memory as the default batch budget is accepted.
  • No streamed quantiles for SGS: quantiles stay in memory (targets x realizations x 8 bytes). When that exceeds the memory budget, simulate raises InvalidInput naming the size needed, before simulating anything.

docs.title: Simulation Output and Parquet Writer Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Simulations always return summary maps and keep only the realizations the user selects (keep=False | True | [indices]), and Parquet files are written several times faster with the same bytes on any thread count.

Architecture: A Keep enum in simulation::post replaces ContinuousOptions::keep: bool and the keep: bool of categorical; summaries carry kept indices beside the kept rows. In ceres-io, a private Encoder replaces ArrowWriter: it slices each batch into row groups, encodes every (row group, column) pair in parallel with rayon, and appends the chunks in order; writer properties pick BYTE_STREAM_SPLIT for floats, DELTA_BINARY_PACKED for the cell index and no dictionary for floats. turning_bands_to_parquet streams kept realizations as columns and hands encoding to a second thread through a depth-1 channel. Python write_parquet releases the GIL, keeps float32 as float32 and writes Arrow batches without concatenating them.

Tech Stack: Rust (parquet 59.3 ArrowRowGroupWriterFactory, arrow 59, rayon), pyo3, numpy, pytest, criterion.

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• License MIT. Conventional commits. Branch + PR to main, never commit to main.
  • No co-author trailers or AI attribution in commits, PRs, issues. PR/issue bodies: a few lines, no sections.
  • PRs ≤ ~400 changed lines (excluding lockfiles).
  • Never name external geostatistics libraries used as inspiration, anywhere.
  • Never commit AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or plan docs (this file stays untracked).
  • Add no dependency for what a few lines do (rayon and criterion are already workspace dependencies).
  • Deterministic parallelism: identical output for any thread count. Parallel map, ordered fold.
  • Errors: one thiserror enum per crate, no anyhow, no panics on user input. Python raises InvalidInput for bad arguments.
  • Every feature ships in Rust and Python together: binding, .pyi stub, NumPy docstrings, one gallery example.
  • No users yet: no deprecation shims, no file-format version bumps.
  • Run everything through mise: mise run build, mise run test, mise run lint, mise run verify, mise run examples.
  • mise run verify must pass before each PR.
  • Minimal docs, no obvious comments, American spelling.

/// Which realizations a summary returns beside its statistics.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Keep {
    /// None: each realization updates the summary, then is freed.
    #[default]
    None,
    /// Every realization.
    All,
    /// These 0-based realizations, returned in realization order.
    Indices(Vec<usize>),
}

impl Keep {
    pub fn keeps(&self, k: usize) -> bool {
        match self {
            Keep::None => false,
            Keep::All => true,
            Keep::Indices(indices) => indices.contains(&k),
        }
    }

    /// The kept realizations of `0..n`, ascending.
    pub fn kept(&self, n: usize) -> Vec<usize> {
        (0..n).filter(|&k| self.keeps(k)).collect()
    }

    /// Every index is below `n` and listed once.
    pub fn validate(&self, n: usize) -> Result<()> {
        let Keep::Indices(indices) = self else {
            return Ok(());
        };
        for (position, &k) in indices.iter().enumerate() {
            if k >= n {
                return Err(SimError::InvalidParameters(format!(
                    "keep lists realization {k}, but there are {n}; indices start at 0"
                )));
            }
            if indices[..position].contains(&k) {
                return Err(SimError::InvalidParameters(format!(
                    "keep lists realization {k} twice"
                )));
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// `keep=`: False, True or 0-based realization indices.
fn keep_arg(keep: Option<&Bound<PyAny>>) -> PyResult<simulation::Keep> {
    let Some(keep) = keep else {
        return Ok(simulation::Keep::None);
    };

        .map(simulation::Keep::Indices)
        .map_err(|_| invalid("keep must be a bool or non-negative realization indices"))
}

use std::sync::Arc;

use arrow_array::{ArrayRef, Float32Array, RecordBatch};
use ceres_core::{BlockModel, Geometry};
use criterion::{Criterion, Throughput, criterion_group, criterion_main};

fn noise(i: u64) -> f32 {
    let mut x = i.wrapping_mul(0x9e3779b97f4a7c15);
    x = (x ^ (x >> 30)).wrapping_mul(0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9);
    x = (x ^ (x >> 27)).wrapping_mul(0x94d049bb133111eb);
    ((x ^ (x >> 31)) >> 40) as f32 / (1u64 << 24) as f32
}

/// 2 000 000 cells with 15 float32 grades, as a simulation writes them.
fn bench(c: &mut Criterion) {
    let count = [200usize, 200, 50];
    let n = count.iter().product::<usize>();
    let columns: Vec<(String, ArrayRef)> = (0..15u64)
        .map(|j| {
            let values = (0..n as u64).map(|i| 2.0 + (i as f32 / 900.0).sin() + noise(i * 16 + j));
            (format!("v{j}"), Arc::new(Float32Array::from_iter_values(values)) as ArrayRef)
        })
        .collect();
    let geometry = Geometry {
        origin: [0.0; 3],
        size: [5.0; 3],
        count: count.map(|c| c as u32),
        rotation: [0.0; 3],
    };
    let model = BlockModel::regular(geometry, RecordBatch::try_from_iter(columns).unwrap()).unwrap();
    let path = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("ceres-bench-{}.parquet", std::process::id()));
    let mut group = c.benchmark_group("parquet");
    group.sample_size(10);
    group.throughput(Throughput::Elements((n * 15) as u64));
    group.bench_function("block model, 2M cells x 15 f32", |b| {
        b.iter(|| ceres_io::write_block_model(&path, &model).unwrap())
    });
    group.finish();
    println!("file size {} MB", std::fs::metadata(&path).unwrap().len() / 1_000_000);
    std::fs::remove_file(path).unwrap();
}

criterion_group!(benches, bench);
criterion_main!(benches);

(Check Geometry::count's element type in crates/core/src/block_model.rs and adjust the map if it is usize.)

use arrow_schema::{DataType, Field, Schema};
use parquet::basic::{Compression, Encoding, ZstdLevel};
use parquet::file::properties::{EnabledStatistics, WriterProperties, WriterVersion};
use parquet::schema::types::ColumnPath;

fn properties(schema: &Schema) -> WriterProperties {
    let mut builder = WriterProperties::builder()
        .set_writer_version(WriterVersion::PARQUET_2_0)
        .set_compression(Compression::ZSTD(ZstdLevel::default()))
        .set_dictionary_enabled(false)
        .set_statistics_enabled(EnabledStatistics::Chunk)
        .set_max_row_group_row_count(Some(ROW_GROUP));
    for field in schema.fields() {
        let path = ColumnPath::from(field.name().as_str());
        builder = match field.data_type() {
            DataType::Float32 | DataType::Float64 => {
                builder.set_column_encoding(path, Encoding::BYTE_STREAM_SPLIT)
            }
            _ if field.name() == INDEX => {
                builder.set_column_encoding(path, Encoding::DELTA_BINARY_PACKED)
            }
            _ => builder.set_column_dictionary_enabled(path, true),
        };
    }
    builder.build()
}

use arrow_schema::SchemaRef;
use parquet::arrow::arrow_writer::{
    ArrowColumnChunk, ArrowColumnWriter, ArrowLeafColumn, ArrowRowGroupWriterFactory,
    compute_leaves,
};
use parquet::file::writer::SerializedFileWriter;
use rayon::prelude::*;

/// A Parquet file whose row groups are encoded column by column in
/// parallel and appended in order, so its bytes do not depend on the
/// number of threads.
struct Encoder {
    file: SerializedFileWriter<File>,
    factory: ArrowRowGroupWriterFactory,
    schema: SchemaRef,
    group: usize,
}

impl Encoder {
    /// A file of row groups of at most `group` rows.
    fn create(file: File, schema: SchemaRef, group: usize) -> Result<Self> {
        let props = properties(&schema);
        let (file, factory) =
            ArrowWriter::try_new(file, schema.clone(), Some(props))?.into_serialized_writer()?;
        Ok(Self {
            file,
            factory,
            schema,
            group,
        })
    }

    /// Appends `batch` as row groups, encoding up to one row group per
    /// thread at a time.
    fn write(&mut self, batch: &RecordBatch) -> Result<()> {
        let rows = batch.num_rows();
        let starts: Vec<usize> = (0..rows).step_by(self.group.max(1)).collect();
        for wave in starts.chunks(rayon::current_num_threads().max(1)) {
            let first = self.file.flushed_row_groups().len();
            let mut jobs: Vec<Vec<(ArrowColumnWriter, ArrowLeafColumn)>> = vec![];
            for (g, &start) in wave.iter().enumerate() {
                let slice = batch.slice(start, self.group.min(rows - start));
                let mut writers = self.factory.create_column_writers(first + g)?.into_iter();
                let mut job = vec![];
                for (field, column) in self.schema.fields().iter().zip(slice.columns()) {
                    for leaf in compute_leaves(field, column)? {
                        job.push((writers.next().expect("one writer per leaf"), leaf));
                    }
                }
                jobs.push(job);
            }
            let groups: Vec<Vec<ArrowColumnChunk>> = jobs
                .into_par_iter()
                .map(|job| {
                    job.into_par_iter()
                        .map(|(mut writer, leaf)| {
                            writer.write(&leaf)?;
                            writer.close()
                        })
                        .collect::<parquet::errors::Result<Vec<_>>>()
                })
                .collect::<parquet::errors::Result<_>>()?;
            for chunks in groups {
                let mut group = self.file.next_row_group()?;
                for chunk in chunks {
                    chunk.append_to_row_group(&mut group)?;
                }
                group.close()?;
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn finish(self) -> Result<()> {
        self.file.close()?;
        Ok(())
    }
}

The wave size depends on the thread count, but it only bounds memory: every row group is encoded on its own and appended in file order, so the bytes don't change. ArrowWriter::try_new(...).into_serialized_writer() keeps the embedded Arrow schema and the ceres metadata exactly as before.

Use it in write:

    let mut encoder = Encoder::create(File::create(path)?, schema, ROW_GROUP)?;
    encoder.write(&batch)?;
    encoder.finish()

In BlockModelWriter, the field writer: Option<ArrowWriter<File>> becomes writer: Option<Encoder>, creation becomes Encoder::create(file, schema, ROW_GROUP)?, and finish calls writer.finish(). Row groups now end at chunk boundaries instead of spanning chunks, which only changes how the rows are split, not the values.

If ? doesn't convert parquet::errors::ParquetError into crate::Error, check crates/io/src/lib.rs for the From impl (there is one already, because ArrowWriter errors use ? today).

Run: mise exec -- cargo test -p simulation streamed Expected: PASS.

  • [ ] Step 2: Implement. Wrap the chunk loop in a scoped thread that owns the writer; the loop sends each finished chunk through a channel of depth 1, so chunk i is encoded while chunk i + 1 simulates:
    let writer = ceres_io::BlockModelWriter::create(
        output,
        *reader.geometry(),
        reader.layout(),
        reader.crs(),
    )?;
    let mut global = GlobalSummary {
        realization_mean: vec![0.0; n],
        realization_above: vec![vec![0.0; n]; options.cutoffs.len()],
    };
    let mut total = 0.0;
    std::thread::scope(|scope| -> Result<()> {
        let (send, receive) = std::sync::mpsc::sync_channel::<ceres_core::BlockModel>(1);
        let writing = scope.spawn(move || -> Result<()> {
            let mut writer = writer;
            for chunk in receive {
                writer.write(&chunk)?;
            }
            writer.finish()?;
            Ok(())
        });
        let simulated = (|| -> Result<()> {
            for chunk in reader.chunks(rows, None)? {
                // ...body unchanged up to building `out`...
                if send.send(out).is_err() {
                    break;
                }
            }
            Ok(())
        })();
        drop(send);
        let written = writing.join().expect("the writer thread does not panic");
        simulated.and(written)
    })?;

The body of the old loop moves inside the closure unchanged, except writer.write(&out)?; becomes the send. When the writer fails, its receiver drops, send fails, the loop stops and the writer's error is returned. The normalization of global after the loop is unchanged. Encoding inside BlockModelWriter::write uses rayon's global pool, as the simulation does; output does not depend on scheduling.

docs.title: Turning Bands at Scale Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Make conditional turning-bands simulation compute each node's neighbours and simple-kriging weights once per batch of realizations instead of once per realization, with results bit-identical to today's per-realization path.

Architecture: A new Conditioning (crates/simulation/src/conditioning.rs) holds, for a tile of nodes, the chosen data and their SK weights. TurningBandsEnsemble::realizations(ks, ..) walks fixed-size tiles of targets in parallel; for each tile it builds the conditioning once (per distinct domain vector of the batch) and applies it to every realization in the batch, reading residuals from a data × realization matrix (realizations contiguous). post::continuous_batched folds batches into the existing Accumulator in realization order. Every caller (summary, realization, turning_bands_to_parquet, Python TurningBands.simulate, multivariate turning-bands factors) moves to the batched path. The unconditional field gets an exact loop reorder (bands outer over a tile of points), and an optional incremental-projection variant gated on a benchmark and on a decision about bit-exactness.

Tech Stack: Rust (rayon, nalgebra), existing estimation::krige, estimation::search::SearchTree, pyo3 bindings in crates/py.

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Output identical for any thread count (AGENTS.md: "Parallelism: rayon, deterministic — identical output for any thread count. Parallel map, ordered fold.").
  • The batched path must equal today's TurningBandsEnsemble::realization bit for bit (compare with ==, which treats -0.0 == 0.0), for every realization, with domains, per-realization domains, soft boundaries, high-grade clamping, trend and nugget. Tasks 1–3 and 6 keep that; only Task 5b may relax it, and only with the user's approval.
  • Summaries must not depend on the realization batch size.
  • Compute in f64. No new dependencies. No unsafe.
  • Every feature ships in Rust and Python together; this plan changes no Python signature, so .pyi stubs and docs stay as they are.

Interfaces: - Consumes: estimation::search::SearchTree::{neighbors_in, cap}, estimation::krige::{krige, Kind}, estimation::Sample. - Produces: - pub(crate) struct Neighbor { pub datum: u32, pub weight: f64, pub cap: Option<f64> } - pub(crate) struct Conditioning - Conditioning::new(targets: &[(f64, f64, f64)], domains: Option<&[u32]>, tree: &SearchTree, data: &[Sample], vg: &Variogram) -> Result<Conditioning> - Conditioning::of(&self, i: usize) -> &[Neighbor] - Conditioning::krige_batch(&self, i: usize, residual: impl Fn(&Neighbor, &mut [f64]), row: &mut [f64], out: &mut [f64]) -> bool

Why the weights are reusable: krige builds its matrix and right-hand side from locations and error_variance only (crates/estimation/src/krige.rs:106-112); values enter only in the final sum. The high-grade cap (SearchTree::cap, crates/estimation/src/search.rs:807) depends on the target, the datum location and the datum's grade, never on the realization, so it changes a residual's value, not the neighbour set or the weights. The residuals condition kriges are Sample::new(loc, value), so error_variance is 0 there too.

Why bit-exactness holds: krige computes mean + Σᵢ wᵢ·(zᵢ − mean) with mean = 0.0 (krige.rs:131). z − 0.0 == z exactly and Iterator::sum for f64 folds from -0.0 in order, so accumulating wᵢ·rᵢ in neighbour order from -0.0 and then adding 0.0 + reproduces it bit for bit.

//! Neighbours and simple-kriging weights of nodes. They depend only on the
//! locations of the nodes and data, so they are found once and applied to
//! the residuals of every realization conditioned from the same data.

use estimation::Sample;
use estimation::krige::{Kind, krige};
use estimation::search::SearchTree;
use variogram::Variogram;

use crate::error::{Result, SimError};

/// Datum `datum` with simple-kriging weight `weight`, its grade capped at
/// `cap` by a clamping high-grade restriction.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
pub(crate) struct Neighbor {
    pub datum: u32,
    pub weight: f64,
    pub cap: Option<f64>,
}

/// The neighbours of each of a run of nodes.
pub(crate) struct Conditioning {
    offsets: Vec<usize>,
    neighbors: Vec<Neighbor>,
}

impl Conditioning {
    /// The data `tree` selects for each of `targets`, of domain `domains[i]`
    /// when given, with their weights in the simple kriging of `vg`; `data`
    /// are the samples the tree was built from.
    pub(crate) fn new(
        targets: &[(f64, f64, f64)],
        domains: Option<&[u32]>,
        tree: &SearchTree,
        data: &[Sample],
        vg: &Variogram,
    ) -> Result<Self> {
        let mut offsets = Vec::with_capacity(targets.len() + 1);
        offsets.push(0);
        let mut neighbors = Vec::new();
        for (i, g) in targets.iter().enumerate() {
            let chosen = tree.neighbors_in(g, domains.map(|d| d[i])).unwrap_or_default();
            if !chosen.is_empty() {
                let near: Vec<Sample> = chosen.iter().map(|&k| Sample::new(data[k].loc, 0.0)).collect();
                let weights = krige(Kind::Simple { mean: 0.0 }, g, &near, vg)
                    .map_err(|e| SimError::Estimation(e.to_string()))?
                    .weights;
                neighbors.extend(chosen.iter().zip(weights).map(|(&k, weight)| Neighbor {
                    datum: k as u32,
                    weight,
                    cap: tree.cap(g, None, k),
                }));
            }
            offsets.push(neighbors.len());
        }
        Ok(Self { offsets, neighbors })
    }

    pub(crate) fn of(&self, i: usize) -> &[Neighbor] {
        &self.neighbors[self.offsets[i]..self.offsets[i + 1]]
    }

    /// The kriged residual of node `i` in each realization of a batch, in
    /// `out`, summed in neighbour order as [`krige`] sums it;
    /// `residual(n, row)` writes neighbour `n`'s residual in each realization
    /// into `row` (as long as `out`). False, leaving `out`, when the node has
    /// no neighbours.
    pub(crate) fn krige_batch(
        &self,
        i: usize,
        residual: impl Fn(&Neighbor, &mut [f64]),
        row: &mut [f64],
        out: &mut [f64],
    ) -> bool {
        let near = self.of(i);
        if near.is_empty() {
            return false;
        }
        out.fill(-0.0);
        for n in near {
            residual(n, row);
            for (o, r) in out.iter_mut().zip(row.iter()) {
                *o += n.weight * r;
            }
        }
        for o in out.iter_mut() {
            *o += 0.0;
        }
        true
    }
}

*o += 0.0 is *o + 0.0; IEEE addition is commutative, signed zeros included, so it equals krige's 0.0 + sum bit for bit. The test's extra 0.0 + out[0] mirrors condition's u + rk with u = 0.0.

    /// Standard-Gaussian unconditional field at `points` (inside the box).
    pub fn field(&self, points: &[(f64, f64, f64)]) -> Vec<f64> {
        points.par_iter().map(|p| self.at(p)).collect()
    }

    /// As [`Bands::field`] on the calling thread.
    fn field_serial(&self, points: &[(f64, f64, f64)]) -> Vec<f64> {

    fn at(&self, p: &(f64, f64, f64)) -> f64 {
        let inv = 1.0 / (self.directions.len() as f64).sqrt();
        let q = self.to_isotropic * Vector3::new(p.0, p.1, p.2);
        let mut sum = 0.0;
        for ((dir, &tmin), band) in self.directions.iter().zip(&self.origins).zip(&self.values) {
            let x = ((q.dot(dir) - tmin) / self.step).max(0.0);
            let i0 = (x.floor() as usize).min(band.len() - 2);
            let frac = x - i0 as f64;
            sum += band[i0] * (1.0 - frac) + band[i0 + 1] * frac;
        }
        if self.nugget > 0.0 {
            sum * inv * (1.0 - self.nugget).sqrt() + white(self.key, p) * self.nugget.sqrt()
        } else {
            sum * inv
        }
    }

    /// Realization `k` at `targets`, of codes `domains` and trend `trend`
    /// when the data have them, back-transformed to data values. Each
    /// realization may take its own `domains`, as simulated domains do.
    pub fn realization(
        &self,
        k: usize,
        targets: &[(f64, f64, f64)],
        domains: Option<&[u32]>,
        trend: Option<&[f64]>,
    ) -> Result<Vec<f64>> {
        Ok(self.realizations(k..k + 1, targets, |_| domains, trend)?.remove(0))
    }

    /// Realizations `ks` at `targets`, each as [`Self::realization`] with
    /// the node domains `domains(k)`. The targets are taken a tile at a
    /// time; a tile's neighbours and kriging weights are found once for
    /// every realization in `ks` that gives it the same domains.
    pub fn realizations<'d>(
        &self,
        ks: std::ops::Range<usize>,
        targets: &[(f64, f64, f64)],
        domains: impl Fn(usize) -> Option<&'d [u32]> + Sync,
        trend: Option<&[f64]>,
    ) -> Result<Vec<Vec<f64>>> {
        if ks.is_empty() || ks.end > self.bands.len() {
            return Err(SimError::InvalidParameters(format!(
                "no realizations {ks:?} among {}",
                self.bands.len()
            )));
        }
        for k in ks.clone() {
            self.transforms(targets.len(), domains(k), trend)?;
        }
        let b = ks.len();
        let mut residuals = vec![0.0; self.data.len() * b];
        for (j, row) in residuals.chunks_mut(b).enumerate() {
            for (r, k) in row.iter_mut().zip(ks.clone()) {
                *r = self.transforms.scores[j] - self.at_data[k][j];
            }
        }
        let tiles: Vec<Vec<Vec<f64>>> = targets
            .par_chunks(TILE)
            .enumerate()
            .map(|(t, tile)| {
                let start = t * TILE;
                let codes = |kk: usize| domains(ks.start + kk).map(|d| &d[start..start + tile.len()]);
                let mut groups: Vec<(Option<&[u32]>, Vec<usize>)> = vec![];
                for kk in 0..b {
                    match groups.iter_mut().find(|(c, _)| *c == codes(kk)) {
                        Some((_, members)) => members.push(kk),
                        None => groups.push((codes(kk), vec![kk])),
                    }
                }
                let mut out = vec![vec![]; b];
                for (codes, members) in groups {
                    let c = Conditioning::new(tile, codes, &self.tree, &self.data, &self.vg)?;
                    let fields: Vec<Vec<f64>> = members
                        .iter()
                        .map(|&kk| self.bands[ks.start + kk].field_serial(tile))
                        .collect();
                    let (mut row, mut rk) = (vec![0.0; members.len()], vec![0.0; members.len()]);
                    for kk in &members {
                        out[*kk] = Vec::with_capacity(tile.len());
                    }
                    for i in 0..tile.len() {
                        let domain = codes.map(|d| d[i]);
                        let residual = |n: &Neighbor, row: &mut [f64]| {
                            let d = n.datum as usize;
                            if n.cap.is_none() && self.data[d].domain == domain {
                                for (r, &kk) in row.iter_mut().zip(&members) {
                                    *r = residuals[d * b + kk];
                                }
                            } else {
                                let s = self.score(d, domain, n.cap);
                                for (r, &kk) in row.iter_mut().zip(&members) {
                                    *r = s - self.at_data[ks.start + kk][d];
                                }
                            }
                        };
                        let found = c.krige_batch(i, residual, &mut row, &mut rk);
                        let at = trend.map_or(0.0, |t| t[start + i]);
                        let transform = self.transforms.domains[domain.unwrap_or(0) as usize]
                            .as_ref()
                            .expect("checked");
                        for (m, &kk) in members.iter().enumerate() {
                            let u = fields[m][i];
                            let score = if found { u + rk[m] } else { u };
                            out[kk].push(transform.back(score, at));
                        }
                    }
                }
                Ok(out)
            })
            .collect::<Result<_>>()?;
        let mut all: Vec<Vec<f64>> = (0..b).map(|_| Vec::with_capacity(targets.len())).collect();
        for tile in tiles {
            for (a, t) in all.iter_mut().zip(tile) {
                a.extend(t);
            }
        }
        Ok(all)
    }

    /// Realizations per batch for `targets` nodes: as many as keep the
    /// batch's values and residuals within [`BATCH_BYTES`], at least one.
    pub fn batch(&self, targets: usize) -> usize {
        let per = (targets + self.data.len()).max(1) * std::mem::size_of::<f64>();
        (BATCH_BYTES / per).clamp(1, self.bands.len().max(1))
    }

pub fn continuous_batched(

    options: &ContinuousOptions,
    batch: usize,
    mut simulate: impl FnMut(std::ops::Range<usize>) -> Result<Vec<Vec<f64>>>,
) -> Result<ContinuousSummary> {
    if n == 0 {
        return Err(SimError::InvalidParameters(
            "need at least one realization".into(),
        ));
    }
    let mut acc = Accumulator::new(n, options)?;
    for start in (0..n).step_by(batch.max(1)) {
        let ks = start..(start + batch.max(1)).min(n);
        let done = simulate(ks.clone())?;
        if done.len() != ks.len() {
            return Err(SimError::InvalidParameters(format!(
                "{} realizations for {} indices",
                done.len(),
                ks.len()
            )));
        }
        done.into_iter().try_for_each(|v| acc.add(v))?;
    }
    Ok(acc.finish())
}

    /// As [`Bands::field`] on the calling thread, band by band over the
    /// points; each point sums its bands in the same order as [`Bands::at`].
    fn field_serial(&self, points: &[(f64, f64, f64)]) -> Vec<f64> {
        let q: Vec<Vector3<f64>> = points
            .iter()
            .map(|p| self.to_isotropic * Vector3::new(p.0, p.1, p.2))
            .collect();
        let mut sum = vec![0.0; points.len()];
        for ((dir, &tmin), band) in self.directions.iter().zip(&self.origins).zip(&self.values) {
            for (s, q) in sum.iter_mut().zip(&q) {
                let x = ((q.dot(dir) - tmin) / self.step).max(0.0);
                let i0 = (x.floor() as usize).min(band.len() - 2);
                let frac = x - i0 as f64;
                *s += band[i0] * (1.0 - frac) + band[i0 + 1] * frac;
            }
        }
        let inv = 1.0 / (self.directions.len() as f64).sqrt();
        sum.iter()
            .zip(points)
            .map(|(s, p)| match self.nugget > 0.0 {
                true => s * inv * (1.0 - self.nugget).sqrt() + white(self.key, p) * self.nugget.sqrt(),
                false => s * inv,
            })
            .collect()
    }

Also make field use it per fixed tile so the public path benefits: points.par_chunks(TILE).flat_map_iter(|c| self.field_serial(c)).collect().

docs.title: Task 5b (gated): Incremental projection along straight runs
docs.text: Do not start without the user's go-ahead. Along a straight, equally spaced run of points (a block-model row), each band's coordinate is an arithmetic progression: t_i = t_0 + i·Δt, one multiply-add per point instead of a dot product. That is not bit-exact: t_0 + i·Δt differs from q_i·dir in the last bits (about 1e-13 absolute on the field), and runs break at tile and chunk boundaries, so a streamed file (rows 4 vs 25) would differ from the in-memory result at that level. Existing tests assert exact equality across chunkings and would need tolerances. Ask the user: accept ~1e-12 differences across chunkings, for a gain to be measured (estimate ≤ 1.5× on the field on top of 5a)? If yes, write it as a separate PR with the gate "≥ 1.3× over 5a on evaluate field".

Files: - Modify: crates/simulation/src/turning_bands.rs — TurningBandsEnsemble gains per-realization seeds and per-realization data values. - Modify: crates/simulation/src/multivariate.rs — a batched multivariate_batched. - Modify: crates/py/src/simulation.rs:2508-2560 — MultivariateSimulation.simulate uses it when every factor is turning bands.

Interfaces: - Consumes: realizations, batch, continuous_batched (Tasks 2–3); factor_seed (multivariate.rs:45). - Produces: - TurningBandsEnsemble::with_realizations(data_locs: &[(f64, f64, f64)], data_vals: &[Vec<f64>], data_weights: Option<&[f64]>, data_holes: Option<&[u32]>, lo: [f64; 3], hi: [f64; 3], vg_nscore: &Variogram, params: &TurningBandsParams, seeds: &[u64]) -> Result<TurningBandsEnsemble> — realization k uses bands seeded seeds[k] and data values data_vals[k] (or data_vals[0] for all when it has one entry). - pub fn multivariate_batched(n: usize, factors: usize, transform: &Decorrelation, options: &ContinuousOptions, support: Option<&BlockSupport>, batch: usize, simulate: impl FnMut(usize, std::ops::Range<usize>) -> Result<Vec<Vec<f64>>>) -> Result<Vec<ContinuousSummary>> — simulate(j, ks) returns factor j's realizations ks.

Today each (realization k, factor j) calls turning_bands(...) with seed = factor_seed(seed, k, j) (py/src/simulation.rs:2548-2555), which builds a one-realization ensemble whose bands are seeded realization_seed(factor_seed(seed, k, j), 0) and whose normal-score transform is fitted to that realization's data values (they differ per realization when impute is used). To be bit-identical, with_realizations must: seed realization k's bands with ceres_core::rng::realization_seed(seeds[k], 0), callers passing seeds[k] = factor_seed(seed, k, j); fit one Transforms per distinct values vector; take the bands' box from lo..hi widened by the data, exactly as new does (turning_bands.rs:526-529). Holding transforms: Vec<Transforms> (one shared, or one per realization) touches score, transforms() and the residual matrix in realizations: index them by realization.

Memory: bands take n_bands × ≤4000 × 8 B ≈ 9.6 MB per realization per factor; 15 factors × 100 realizations ≈ 14 GB if all are built up front. So multivariate_batched builds each factor's ensemble per realization batch (seeds[ks], data_vals[ks]), uses it, and drops it. Weights are then recomputed once per batch per factor, which the batch size keeps rare.

Then:

    /// As [`Self::new`] without domains or trend, realization `k` drawn
    /// from seed `seeds[k]` with data values `data_vals[k]` (one entry: the
    /// same values for all), as a one-realization ensemble seeded
    /// `seeds[k]` would draw it.
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub fn with_realizations(
        data_locs: &[(f64, f64, f64)],
        data_vals: &[Vec<f64>],
        data_weights: Option<&[f64]>,
        data_holes: Option<&[u32]>,
        lo: [f64; 3],
        hi: [f64; 3],
        vg_nscore: &Variogram,
        params: &TurningBandsParams,
        seeds: &[u64],
    ) -> Result<Self> {
        if data_vals.is_empty() || (data_vals.len() != 1 && data_vals.len() != seeds.len()) {
            return Err(SimError::InvalidParameters(
                "one values vector, or one per realization".into(),
            ));
        }
        if data_vals.iter().any(|v| v.len() != data_locs.len()) {
            return Err(SimError::InvalidParameters("data length mismatch".into()));
        }
        if data_locs.is_empty() {
            return Err(SimError::InsufficientData("no conditioning data".into()));
        }
        let holes = crate::holes(data_holes, data_locs.len())?;
        let transforms = data_vals
            .iter()
            .map(|v| Transforms::fit(v, data_weights, None, None))
            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
        let (dlo, dhi) = bounds(data_locs);
        let lo = std::array::from_fn(|i| lo[i].min(dlo[i]));
        let hi = std::array::from_fn(|i| hi[i].max(dhi[i]));
        let layout = Layout::new(lo, hi, vg_nscore, params);
        let (bands, at_data): (Vec<Bands>, Vec<Vec<f64>>) = seeds
            .par_iter()
            .map(|&s| {
                let mut rng = StdRng::seed_from_u64(ceres_core::rng::realization_seed(s, 0));
                let bands = layout.bands(params.n_bands, &mut rng);
                let at_data = bands.field(data_locs);
                (bands, at_data)
            })
            .unzip();
        let data = data(data_locs, &data_vals[0], holes, None);
        let tree = SearchTree::new(&data, &params.search, Some(vg_nscore));
        Ok(Self {
            transforms,
            data,
            trend: None,
            bands,
            at_data,
            tree,
            vg: vg_nscore.clone(),
        })
    }

The accumulators are private to post.rs, so first add there, after continuous_many:

/// As [`continuous_many`], `batch` realizations at a time: `simulate(ks)`
/// returns, for each realization of `ks` in order, every variable.
pub fn continuous_many_batched(
    n: usize,
    variables: usize,
    options: &ContinuousOptions,
    batch: usize,
    mut simulate: impl FnMut(std::ops::Range<usize>) -> Result<Vec<Vec<Vec<f64>>>>,
) -> Result<Vec<ContinuousSummary>> {
    if n == 0 {
        return Err(SimError::InvalidParameters(
            "need at least one realization".into(),
        ));
    }
    let mut accs = (0..variables)
        .map(|_| Accumulator::new(n, options))
        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
    for start in (0..n).step_by(batch.max(1)) {
        let ks = start..(start + batch.max(1)).min(n);
        let done = simulate(ks.clone())?;
        if done.len() != ks.len() {
            return Err(SimError::InvalidParameters(format!(
                "{} realizations for {} indices",
                done.len(),
                ks.len()
            )));
        }
        for values in done {
            if values.len() != variables {
                return Err(SimError::InvalidParameters(format!(
                    "one realization per variable ({variables}) needed"
                )));
            }
            accs.iter_mut().zip(values).try_for_each(|(a, v)| a.add(v))?;
        }
    }
    Ok(accs.into_iter().map(Accumulator::finish).collect())
}

Export it from lib.rs next to continuous_batched. Then in crates/simulation/src/multivariate.rs:

/// As [`multivariate`], `batch` realizations at a time: `simulate(j, ks)`
/// returns realizations `ks` of factor `j` at the nodes.
pub fn multivariate_batched(
    n: usize,
    factors: usize,
    transform: &Decorrelation,
    options: &ContinuousOptions,
    support: Option<&BlockSupport>,
    batch: usize,
    mut simulate: impl FnMut(usize, std::ops::Range<usize>) -> Result<Vec<Vec<f64>>>,
) -> Result<Vec<ContinuousSummary>> {
    crate::post::continuous_many_batched(n, factors, options, batch, |ks| {
        let columns = (0..factors)
            .map(|j| simulate(j, ks.clone()))
            .collect::<Result<Vec<Vec<Vec<f64>>>>>()?;
        (0..ks.len())
            .map(|kk| {
                let nodes = columns.first().map_or(0, |c| c[kk].len());
                let rows: Vec<Vec<f64>> = (0..nodes)
                    .map(|i| columns.iter().map(|c| c[kk][i]).collect())
                    .collect();
                let back = transform.back(&rows);
                (0..factors)
                    .map(|v| {
                        let values: Vec<f64> = back.iter().map(|r| r[v]).collect();
                        match support {
                            Some(s) => s.mean(&values),
                            None => Ok(values),
                        }
                    })
                    .collect()
            })
            .collect()
    })
}

docs.title: Self-review notes
docs.text:
• Coverage: chunk-major conditioning (Tasks 1–2), residuals data × realization contiguous (Task 2), per-domain and per-realization domains (Task 2 grouping), caps verified to change values not weights (Task 1 rationale + regression test with HighGradeMode::Clamp), streaming summaries and keep (Task 3, plan 1 compatible), realization batching by memory (Task 2 batch, Task 3), deterministic fixed TILE (Task 2), incremental field along rows (Tasks 5a exact / 5b gated), multivariate factors (Task 6), benchmarks (Task 4).
  • The "small GEMM" is realized as the per-node loop over neighbours with realizations innermost and contiguous (krige_batch); a reordered GEMM would break bit-exactness, which the constraints forbid.
  • Masked and sub-blocked models need no special path: tiles are index ranges over whatever targets arrive.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
1. Task 5b: may the field differ at ~1e-12 between chunkings (in-memory vs streamed rows) for an incremental projection? Default in this plan: no, keep bit-exactness.
  2. Task 6: with impute and a high-grade restriction, grades differ per realization, so the selection itself would differ. The plan rejects that combination with an error in the batched path and keeps the old path for it. Acceptable, or should it fall back silently to the per-realization path?
  3. BATCH_BYTES = 1 GiB and multivariate batch = 8 are fixed; should they follow available memory (plan 4 plans memory-driven batches for SGS) or a user argument?
  4. Bands memory: TurningBandsEnsemble::new still builds bands for all n realizations up front (~9.6 MB each, ~1 GB at n = 100). Streaming (turning_bands_to_parquet) needs them all per chunk. Storing band values as f32 would halve it but break bit-exactness; left out.

In post.rs: stored: Vec<f32> becomes stored: Vec<f64>; in add, self.stored.extend(values.iter().map(|&v| v as f32)); becomes self.stored.extend_from_slice(&values);; in finish, stored[r * m + i] as f64 becomes stored[r * m + i].

Run: mise exec -- cargo test -p simulation post Expected: PASS, including the existing quantile_values tests.

  • [ ] Step 3: Failing test: a streamed run with quantiles stays within the memory budget

Add to the turning_bands.rs tests:

    #[test]
    fn quantile_chunks_fit_the_budget() {
        assert_eq!(quantile_rows(1_000_000, 100, 0), 1_000_000);
        assert_eq!(quantile_rows(1_000_000, 100, 3), (BATCH_BYTES / (100 * 8)).min(1_000_000));
        assert_eq!(quantile_rows(1_000_000, 1 << 40, 3), 1);
    }

Run: mise exec -- cargo test -p simulation quantile_chunks_fit_the_budget Expected: FAIL to compile: quantile_rows not found.

  • [ ] Step 4: Cap the chunk

Add in turning_bands.rs next to BATCH_BYTES:

/// Blocks per streamed chunk: `rows`, fewer when quantiles keep every
/// realization of the chunk, so they stay within [`BATCH_BYTES`].
fn quantile_rows(rows: usize, n: usize, quantiles: usize) -> usize {
    match quantiles {
        0 => rows,
        _ => rows.min(BATCH_BYTES / (n.max(1) * 8)).max(1),
    }
}

In turning_bands_to_parquet, before the second for chunk in reader.chunks(rows, None)? loop, add let rows = quantile_rows(rows, n, options.quantiles.len());.

Run: mise exec -- cargo test -p simulation turning_bands Expected: PASS, including the streamed tests that compare rows 4 vs 25 with the in-memory summary (quantiles do not depend on the chunking).

docs.text:
• Memory: BATCH_BYTES = 1 GiB and the multivariate batch = 8 stay as defaults.
  • Quantiles stream for turning bands only (Task 7): exact, f64, chunk capped to the memory budget.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Long-running Rust computations exposed to Python (kriging/estimation, SGS/SIS simulation, I/O, mesh and implicit-modelling) already run in parallel via rayon but give no feedback while running. Add a tqdm-backed progress bar, on by default, with no change to output.

Out of scope: new parallelism, GPU acceleration. Rayon already covers parallelism project-wide; GPU is not justified by any benchmark today (per AGENTS.md).

docs.title: Core mechanism (ceres-core)
docs.text:
pub struct Progress {
    done: AtomicU64,
    total: Option<u64>, // None = indeterminate (CSV/GSLIB reads: total unknown upfront)
}
impl Progress {
    pub fn new(total: Option<u64>) -> Self
    pub fn inc(&self)             // Relaxed fetch_add, called once per unit inside the rayon loop
    pub fn snapshot(&self) -> (u64, Option<u64>)
}
inc() is a side-channel counter only — it never participates in the actual parallel reduction/output, so the "identical output for any thread count" guarantee is untouched.

Each targeted function gains one new parameter, progress: Option<&Progress> in Rust, defaulting to None for existing Rust/test/bench callers (no behavior change there).

docs.title: Entry points in scope
docs.text:
• Estimation (crates/py/src/estimation.rs, cokriging.rs, indicator.rs, categorical.rs): predict, parallel over targets — total known upfront.
  • Simulation (crates/py/src/simulation.rs): simulate, simulate_to_parquet (SGS/SIS), parallel over realizations — total known upfront.
  • I/O (crates/py/src/io.rs): read_csv, write_csv, read_gslib, write_gslib, read_parquet, write_parquet, read_mesh, write_mesh. Parquet/mesh/writes know their total row/element count upfront; CSV/GSLIB reads don't without a pre-scan, so they use total=None (indeterminate tqdm counter, no percentage/ETA).
  • Modeling (crates/py/src/modeling.rs): implicit/RBF fit and isosurface extraction. modeling gains a direct ceres-core dependency (already available transitively via estimation; this just makes it direct).

Out of scope: multigaussian.rs and transforms.rs predict (anamorphosis-style transforms) — not kriging/simulation/IO/mesh.

docs.title: Python integration
docs.text:
One shared helper, crates/py/src/progress.rs: 

pub fn with_progress<T: Send>(
    py: Python<'_>,
    total: Option<u64>,
    show: bool,
    f: impl FnOnce(Option<&ceres_core::Progress>) -> T + Send,
) -> PyResult<T>
- show = false: py.allow_threads(|| f(None)) — identical to today, zero overhead. - show = true: builds a tqdm.tqdm(total=total) bar, spawns one monitor thread that wakes every ~50ms, reads the shared Progress counter and calls bar.update(delta) under the GIL, while the real computation runs via py.allow_threads(|| f(Some(&counter))) on the calling thread (GIL free for the monitor). The monitor is signalled to exit immediately once the computation finishes (not on its next fixed tick), so fast/synthetic calls aren't slowed down. Final flush + bar.close() on completion.

Every entry point in scope is wired through this one helper — no per-crate reimplementation.

Signature: each gets a keyword-only progress: bool = True (#[pyo3(signature = (..., progress=true))]; thin Python wrappers that already spell out kwargs explicitly, e.g. OrdinaryKriging.predict in estimation.py, get it added and passed through the same way as return_variance/diagnostics).

Dependency: tqdm becomes a core dependency (pyproject.toml dependencies), not an extra — AGENTS.md's "Required dep: numpy only" line is updated to reflect this.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text: The monitor thread only calls bar.update()/bar.close(). If that Python call ever raises (essentially never), it's logged via err.print(py) and the monitor stops — a cosmetic failure never aborts or masks the result of the real computation.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• ceres-core: unit test for Progress (inc/snapshot).
  • pytest: one test per category (a kriging predict, one simulate, read_csv, read_mesh, isosurface) asserting progress=True and progress=False produce bit-identical output — the one runnable check backing "side-channel only".

docs.title: True-edge section plots for block model validation
Goal
docs.text:
Postpone plot3d.py (pyvista 3D). Focus instead on 2D section plots that let a user check a block model against the data it was built from: true block-cell edges (not a resampled raster, so sub-blocked models show their real geometry), the estimate on those blocks, lens/domain surfaces, and drillhole composites — all on one plate, on one colour scale — plus a documented pattern for checking composite-vs-block adherence.

Out of scope: any new spatial-join/adherence core function, slab()'s signature or behaviour, true edges for a cutting plane not aligned to the model's own axes, and anything 3D/pyvista.

docs.title: What already exists (reused, not rebuilt)
docs.text:
• Global domain-vs-composite statistics: validate_model() (crates/eda).
  • Local: swath() (crates/eda) + plot.swath() — already generic over any two paired series (composites, blocks) with the same bin width.
  • Overlay primitives: plot.slab() already draws points (composites), mesh traces (lenses, via _trace), and clipped polylines (drillhole traces, via _clip) on an arbitrary plane = (center, azimuth, dip), coloured by a scheme.
  • Point-in-block lookup: BlockModel.row_at(points) — the only primitive adherence checking needs.

The gap is plot.section(): it resamples a block model onto an imshow raster via to_regular(), which loses true sub-block edges, and its axis/index path explicitly ignores the model's rotation.

docs.title: Rust: BlockModel.corners()
docs.text:
crates/core/src/block_model.rs, next to centroids()/volumes():

/// World-space corners of each row's box: 8 vertices (every combination of its
/// local u, v, w min/max), rotation-aware. `(n, 8, 3)` flattened per row.
pub fn corners(&self) -> Vec<[[f64; 3]; 8]>

Computed via Geometry::point(index, at) (already used by centroid/locate) at the 8 corner combinations of each row's local extent — [0,0,0]..[1,1,1] for regular/masked rows, the row's fractional extent for sub-blocked rows. No new geometry math, just the existing affine transform applied at box corners instead of the center.

Exposed to Python (crates/py/src/containers.rs) as a corners property, (n, 8, 3) float64, same pattern as centroids/extents; .pyi stub added.

Theory check: for every row, the parallelepiped volume computed from corners() (triple product of its three edge vectors from one vertex) equals model.volumes()[row], within tolerance — proptest over regular, masked, and sub-blocked layouts, rotated and unrotated.

docs.title: Python: section() internals change, signature does not
docs.text:
section(model, values, *, axis="z", index=None, plane=None, resolution=None, colorbar=True, scheme=None, ax=None, **kwargs) — unchanged parameters.

  • Resolve the cutting plane (from axis/index, or from an explicit plane) through the same _frame(plane)/_label() helpers slab() already uses, so a plane tuple means the same u/v convention and axis labels in both functions.
  • If that plane is parallel to two of the model's own local axes — always true for the axis/index path by construction; checkable for an explicit plane by comparing its azimuth/dip against model.rotation within tolerance — draw true block rectangles from corners() as a PatchCollection (filled, no stroked edges; large collections rasterize fine without per-edge strokes) instead of resampling.
  • Otherwise (a plane at a genuine angle to the model), keep today's raster imshow fallback unchanged.
  • Side effect: the axis/index path now honours model.rotation (today's docstring says "rotation ignored" — that was a real limitation for rotated deposits, fixed by routing through _frame like slab() does).

No new parameters on section(). Overlays (lenses, drillhole composites) are not added here — see below.

docs.title: Composing the validation plate: overlap plots on one ax
docs.text:
section() and slab() already share the contract of taking ax= and returning (fig, ax). Composing them is two calls on the same ax with the same plane tuple, not a merged signature:

plane = (center, azimuth, dip)  # aligned to the model's own frame, for true edges
fig, ax = cs.plot.section(model, "TREO_OK", plane=plane, scheme=domains)
cs.plot.slab(composites, "TREO_PPM", plane=plane, thickness=25, meshes=lens_mesh,
             lines=drillhole_traces, scheme=domains, ax=ax)

The same scheme on both calls keeps blocks and composites on one colour scale.

docs.title: Adherence: a documented pattern, no new function
docs.text:
row_at() already maps world points to containing-block rows:

rows = model.row_at(composites.coords)
paired = rows >= 0

then cs.plot.scatter(model["TREO_OK"][rows[paired]], composites["TREO_PPM"][paired]) gives the 1:1 line + regression slope (conditional bias), and cs.plot.conditional(...) gives the binned mean/P10–P90 view. Both already exist and already do what "adherence" needs. The only new artifact is a gallery example showing the pairing once, so it is discoverable.

docs.title: Testing & delivery
docs.text:
• Rust: corners() shape + hand-checked corner positions (axis-aligned, then rotated); proptest volume-from-corners theory check across layouts.
  • Python: section()'s alignment-detection branch (aligned → patches, misaligned → raster still used); a rotated-model regression test that axis/index places blocks where plane-based slab() places the equivalent overlay.
  • Gallery: one new examples/ topic showing section() (true edges, sub-blocked model)
  • slab() (lens mesh trace + drillhole composites) on one ax, plus the adherence scatter pattern above.
  • Docs: NumPy docstring updates for section() (rotation honoured, true edges when aligned) and the new corners(); .pyi stub for corners().

regularize(target, *, min_fraction=0.0)

Columns of this model averaged onto the blocks of target.

Each row of this model counts in a target block by the volume they share, from exact box overlaps, so it works both ways between regular, masked and sub-blocked models: to a coarser grid, sub-blocks to their parents, or a regular estimate onto sub-blocks.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default target BlockModel

Blocks to average onto, with the same rotation (the origin and sizes may differ). Its own columns are kept.

required min_fraction float

0.0

Returns:

Type Description BlockModel

target with every column of this model: floats as volume-weighted means of the non-null rows, other columns (text, integers) as the value filling the most volume, ties to the smallest, nulls not voting. fraction is the share of each block covered by this model, so volumes * fraction * grade sums to this model's volumes * grade.

subblock(meshes, subgrid, *, column='domain', fill=None)

Sub-blocks every block by prioritized meshes.

Polylines take "inside" only: the vertical prism over their features, as Polylines.contains.

Name of the label column.

Label of the sub-cells no domain holds; without it they are dropped.

None

    inline_byte=189,
    crossline_byte=193,
    x_byte=181,
    y_byte=185,
    nodata=None,
)

Reads a post-stack SEG-Y cube as a 3D BlockModel.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str or Path

A SEG-Y file with one trace per inline and crossline, in sample format 1 (IBM float), 2, 3, 5, 6, 8, 10, 11 or 16 and either byte order.

required column str

Name of the float32 column holding the samples.

"amplitude" inline_byte int

1-based trace-header bytes of the 4-byte inline and crossline numbers.

189 and 193 crossline_byte int

1-based trace-header bytes of the 4-byte inline and crossline numbers.

189 and 193 x_byte int

1-based trace-header bytes of the 4-byte CDP x and y, scaled by the coordinate scalar at byte 71 (negative divides).

181 and 185 y_byte int

1-based trace-header bytes of the 4-byte CDP x and y, scaled by the coordinate scalar at byte 71 (negative divides).

181 and 185 nodata float

Sample value read as null. NaN samples are always null.

None

Returns:

Type Description BlockModel

A regular grid with x along the inlines and y along the crosslines, each from the smallest to the largest line number in steps of the gcd of their gaps; positions without a trace are null. Cell sizes, origin and azimuth (that of the crossline axis) are a least-squares fit of the CDP coordinates; a left-handed survey has its inlines reversed. z is minus the sample time (ms) or depth, the sample interval divided by 1000, so the first sample is the top cell.

Raises:

Type Description InvalidInput

For truncated or non-SEG-Y files, unsupported sample formats, two traces at one position (prestack gathers) and skewed surveys.

docs.title: write_segy builtin
docs.text:
write_segy(path, model, column, *, nodata=0.0)

Writes one column of a BlockModel as SEG-Y revision 1.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str or Path

The .sgy file: big-endian IEEE floats (format 5), an EBCDIC textual header and one trace per (x, y) column.

required model BlockModel

A regular or masked grid rotated by azimuth only. Inline i + 1 and crossline j + 1 go to trace bytes 189 and 193 and the cell-center CDP x and y to bytes 181 and 185. The cell height times 1000 is the sample interval and minus the top cell-center z the delay; both must be stored exactly.

required column str

Numeric column to write, as float32, top cell first.

required nodata float

Value written for nulls and absent cells of a masked model.

0.0

Raises:

Type Description InvalidInput

For sub-blocked models, dip or rake rotations, missing or text columns, and cell heights or tops that SEG-Y cannot hold exactly.

Mesh Triangulated surface or solid with per-vertex and per-face attributes. Polylines Lines and polygons with one attribute row per feature. read_csv Reads a headed CSV; numbers become float64, nodata values become null. write_csv Writes a headed CSV. read_gslib Reads a GSLIB file; the title is kept in the schema metadata and nodata values, as in read_csv, become null. write_gslib Writes numeric columns as GSLIB; nulls are written as nodata. read_segy Reads a post-stack SEG-Y cube as a 3D BlockModel. write_segy Writes one column of a BlockModel as SEG-Y revision 1.

docs.title: datasets
docs.text:
Example datasets, downloaded once from a pinned commit and checked by SHA-256.

Files are cached under $BOITATA_DATA, else the user cache directory (%LOCALAPPDATA%/boitata on Windows, $XDG_CACHE_HOME/boitata or ~/.cache/boitata elsewhere). Coordinates are local metres (Jura: km) with no CRS, except F3 (EPSG:23031). Synthetic datasets are CC BY 4.0; classic ones keep their original terms.

Smallest regular grid holding every object plus a buffer.

Parameters:

What the grid must cover: points, drill hole paths, mesh or line vertices, the corners of another grid, or (n, 2)/(n, 3) coordinates.

0.0 rotation tuple of float

Azimuth, dip and rake in degrees; the extents are measured along the rotated grid axes.

None snap bool, float or sequence of float

Put the origin on a multiple of this step, measured along the grid axes, so grids built from different data line up; True snaps to the block size.

False crs str None

docs.title: regularize method descriptor
docs.text:
regularize(target, *, min_fraction=0.0)

Columns of this model averaged onto the blocks of target.

Each row of this model counts in a target block by the volume they share, from exact box overlaps, so it works both ways between regular, masked and sub-blocked models: to a coarser grid, sub-blocks to their parents, or a regular estimate onto sub-blocks.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default target BlockModel

Blocks to average onto, with the same rotation (the origin and sizes may differ). Its own columns are kept.

required min_fraction float

Blocks less covered than this are null.

0.0

Returns:

Type Description BlockModel

target with every column of this model: floats as volume-weighted means of the non-null rows, other columns (text, integers) as the value filling the most volume, ties to the smallest, nulls not voting. fraction is the share of each block covered by this model, so volumes * fraction * grade sums to this model's volumes * grade.

docs.title: subblock method descriptor
docs.text:
subblock(meshes, subgrid, *, column='domain', fill=None)

Sub-blocks every block by prioritized meshes.

Each block is split on a regular subgrid; each sub-cell takes the label of the first domain holding its center. Blocks of one label stay whole, others keep runs of sub-cells merged along x, then y.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default meshes sequence of (Mesh or Polylines, str, str)

(mesh, rule, label) in priority order, the first match winning. rule is "inside" a closed mesh, or "below" or "above" a surface such as topography, along world z; off the surface's footprint neither matches. Polylines take "inside" only: the vertical prism over their features, as Polylines.contains.

required subgrid int or sequence of int

Sub-cells per axis, which sets the smallest sub-block; an int applies to x, y and z, or to x and y only in a 2D model.

required column str

Name of the label column.

"domain" fill str

Label of the sub-cells no domain holds; without it they are dropped.

None

Returns:

Type Description BlockModel

Sub-blocked model on subgrid with the label column and the columns of each sub-block's parent block.

docs.title: read_segy builtin
docs.text:
read_segy(
    path,
    *,
    column="amplitude",
    inline_byte=189,
    crossline_byte=193,
    x_byte=181,
    y_byte=185,
    nodata=None,
)

Reads a post-stack SEG-Y cube as a 3D BlockModel.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str or Path

A SEG-Y file with one trace per inline and crossline, in sample format 1 (IBM float), 2, 3, 5, 6, 8, 10, 11 or 16 and either byte order.

required column str

Name of the float32 column holding the samples.

"amplitude" inline_byte int

1-based trace-header bytes of the 4-byte inline and crossline numbers.

189 and 193 crossline_byte int

1-based trace-header bytes of the 4-byte inline and crossline numbers.

189 and 193 x_byte int

1-based trace-header bytes of the 4-byte CDP x and y, scaled by the coordinate scalar at byte 71 (negative divides).

181 and 185 y_byte int

1-based trace-header bytes of the 4-byte CDP x and y, scaled by the coordinate scalar at byte 71 (negative divides).

181 and 185 nodata float

Sample value read as null. NaN samples are always null.

None

Returns:

Type Description BlockModel

A regular grid with x along the inlines and y along the crosslines, each from the smallest to the largest line number in steps of the gcd of their gaps; positions without a trace are null. Cell sizes, origin and azimuth (that of the crossline axis) are a least-squares fit of the CDP coordinates; a left-handed survey has its inlines reversed. z is minus the sample time (ms) or depth, the sample interval divided by 1000, so the first sample is the top cell.

Raises:

Type Description InvalidInput

For truncated or non-SEG-Y files, unsupported sample formats, two traces at one position (prestack gathers) and skewed surveys.

regularize(target, *, min_fraction=0.0)

Columns of this model averaged onto the blocks of target.

Each row of this model counts in a target block by the volume they share, from exact box overlaps, so it works both ways between regular, masked and sub-blocked models: to a coarser grid, sub-blocks to their parents, or a regular estimate onto sub-blocks.

Parameters:

Blocks to average onto, with the same rotation (the origin and sizes may differ). Its own columns are kept.

required min_fraction float

Blocks less covered than this are null.

0.0

Returns:

Type Description BlockModel

target with every column of this model: floats as volume-weighted means of the non-null rows, other columns (text, integers) as the value filling the most volume, ties to the smallest, nulls not voting. fraction is the share of each block covered by this model, so volumes * fraction * grade sums to this model's volumes * grade.

Sub-blocks every block by prioritized meshes.

Each block is split on a regular subgrid; each sub-cell takes the label of the first domain holding its center. Blocks of one label stay whole, others keep runs of sub-cells merged along x, then y.

Polylines take "inside" only: the vertical prism over their features, as Polylines.contains.

mesh_intervals(mesh, *, step=1.0, tolerance=0.01)

Splits each hole's path against a closed mesh, wherever it crosses the surface.

The path is sampled every step of depth and a crossing between two samples is bisected down to tolerance; a boundary crossed more than once within one step is missed. Every depth down every hole falls in exactly one row, so piping the result through merge_intervals splits assays exactly at the mesh instead of at a logged contact.

Parameters:

A closed mesh.

required step float

Sampling step down each hole, in meters.

1.0 tolerance float

Depth tolerance the crossing is refined to, in meters.

0.01

runs(

    *,
    cutoff=None,
    category=None,
    ore=Ellipsis,
    min_length=0.0,
    max_dilution=0.0,
    edge=0.0,
)

Ore and waste runs down each hole: contiguous intervals above cutoff (or of an ore category), cleaned by mining rules. The runs of a hole partition its samples, so Σ grade × length equals the sample metal.

Rules apply in order: internal dilution, then edge dilution, then minimum length. Samples missing the grade are left out, as unsampled ground, and samples missing the category are waste; like composite(None, ...), gaps are skipped, not bridged.

Column whose values in ore flag ore samples.

Ore values of category.

Runs spanning less, shortest first, take their neighbors' flag and merge with them.

Waste runs between ore spanning at most this are taken into the ore when the grade of the three together stays at or above cutoff.

Waste taken into each ore run on each side where it meets waste.

0.0

docs.title: GaussianImputer
docs.text:
Imputes missing variables from the variables present in the same sample and, with spatial, from nearby samples.

Each variable is normal-scored on its observed values; the mean and covariance of the scores are fitted by expectation-maximization, missing entries included. Each missing score is drawn from its Gaussian distribution given the scores present in its row and back-transformed, so the imputed values keep the histograms and correlations of the data.

With spatial, the scores follow an intrinsic model: every variable and pair of variables shares the correlogram of spatial, scaled by the score covariance (of the row's component, with a mixture). Rows are visited along a random path and their missing scores drawn by simple cokriging from the scores in the row and in the nearest samples, imputed ones included.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default components int or None

Gaussians mixed in the scores, e.g. 2 for two mineral associations that one Gaussian cannot represent; None picks 1 to 6 by BIC. A missing score is then drawn from a component picked by its probability given the scores present in the row.

1 seed int

Seed of the mixture and of the draws; the same seed imputes the same values.

0 spatial Variogram

Normal-score variogram shared by all variables; its sill is rescaled to one. A pure nugget imputes as without spatial.

required neighbors int

Nearest samples, in the variogram's anisotropic distance, that each draw conditions on; those beyond the range are left out.

16

    *,

    rotation=None,

)

One anisotropic model fitted jointly to experimental variograms in several directions.

The structures share the anisotropy; their ranges are major-axis ranges. Nugget, sills and ranges are free, fixed or bounded as in Variogram.fit, and so is each angle and range ratio. Free ranges stay within the largest lag; bound them, e.g. ranges=[None, (50, 300)], to go further. The search is deterministic.

Azimuth, dip and rake in degrees; free angles are returned with azimuth and rake in [0, 180).

None ratios sequence of (None, float or (float, float))

Semi-major/major and minor/major range ratios, in (0, 1] when free. When every direction is horizontal, dip and rake default to 0 and the minor ratio to 1: the fit is two-dimensional.

Direction and cone half-angle in degrees; omnidirectional when azimuth is None.

None dip float

Direction and cone half-angle in degrees; omnidirectional when azimuth is None.

None tolerance float

Direction and cone half-angle in degrees; omnidirectional when azimuth is None.

None bandwidth float

Largest offset of a pair from the direction line.

None estimator (matheron, cressie - hawkins, covariance, correlogram, pairwise - relative, madogram)

Classical, robust, σ² − C(h), 1 − ρ(h), the pairwise-relative variogram (non-negative values only), or the madogram Σ |Δz| / 2N, in the units of the values: √(γ/π) for Gaussian increments and less sensitive than γ to a few extreme pairs (see dissemination).

"matheron" standardize bool

Divide by the sample variance so the sill is 1, the madogram by the standard deviation. The correlogram and pairwise-relative estimates are dimensionless and left unchanged; a cross-variogram is divided by σ₁σ₂.

False other (array_like, shape(m))

Second variable, for its cross-variogram with values: "matheron" gives γ₁₂(h) = Σ Δz₁·Δz₂ / 2N, "covariance" gives C₁₂(0) − C₁₂(h) with C₁₂(h) in covariances. C₁₂(h) pairs values at the tail with other at the head, so the directional cone is one-sided: reversing azimuth estimates C₂₁(h); omnidirectional averages both.

None other_coords (array_like, shape(m, 2) or (m, 3))

Where other is sampled when not at coords. Only the cross-covariance is defined then, with C₁₂(0) estimated from the pairs closer than half a lag.

None holes (array_like, shape(n))

Hole id of each sample, for a downhole variogram: only pairs in the same hole count, lag k gathers the pairs within lag / 2 of k * lag and reports their mean distance. With azimuth, only the pairs inside the direction cone count, e.g. the flat stretches of bent holes. Not with other.

None method (None, pairs, grid)

How pairs are found. "pairs" compares every two samples, O(n²). "grid" needs a regular or masked BlockModel: every pair of cells one index offset apart has the same separation, so each offset within max_lag and the direction cone is binned once and its pairs are gathered by shifting cell indices, O(n x offsets), with the same pairs and estimates as "pairs" up to round-off; offsets exactly on a lag or cone boundary are decided once, where round-off can split their pairs in the search. None takes "grid" for such a BlockModel without holes or other_coords, else "pairs".

None anisotropy LocalAnisotropy

Local frames: each pair's separation is read in the frame of the nearest location to its tail, and azimuth and dip are relative to it (azimuth 0 the local major axis, 90 the semi-major, dip 90 the minor), so the cone follows a folded or rotating continuity. Pairs come from "pairs"; not with other or holes.

None

Returns:

Type Description ExperimentalVariogram

Degree of dissemination per lag, √π · M(h) / √γ(h).

docs.text: Name Summary Structure One nested structure: sill is the partial sill, range the range along the major axis. Variogram Nugget plus nested structures sharing one anisotropy. ExperimentalVariogram Lag centers, semivariances and pair counts; covariances holds C(h) for the covariance estimator, ρ(h) for the correlogram, and is None otherwise. experimental_variogram Experimental variogram, omnidirectional unless azimuth is given, or the cross-variogram of values and other. dissemination Degree of dissemination per lag, √π · M(h) / √γ(h). docs.title: Search
docs.text: Neighborhood: radius is in meters along the major axis of the search ellipsoid (rotation azimuth, dip, rake and ratios semi/major, minor/major), or of the variogram's anisotropy when no ellipsoid is given. octant takes at most max_samples / 8 samples from each octant around the target, split along the ellipsoid's axes; with 2D data (one elevation) the sectors are the ellipse's four quadrants, max_samples / 4 each. high_grade, a HighGrade or (threshold, radius), restricts samples above threshold to targets within radius, measured in the same ellipsoid unless the HighGrade has its own, in estimation and cross-validation alike; give each pass its own to vary it by pass. The threshold is always in data units: simulators compare it with the data values and the simulated values of nodes, so it picks the same samples as in estimation. Estimators also take a sequence of searches as passes: targets one leaves unestimated go to the next. soft lets samples of another domain inform a target strictly within a distance in the same ellipsoid: one distance for every pair of domains, or a dict {(target_domain, sample_domain): distance}, one way; pairs not listed are hard.

cross_validate(

Re-estimates every sample from the others, through the same search passes.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default folds int

Leave-one-out when None; otherwise k-fold, each sample estimated without the samples of its fold. Samples fitted with holes keep their holes whole: the j-th of the sorted hole ids goes to fold j % folds. None error_variance array_like or str

Variance of each sample's measurement error, for data of different quality (kriging only). None domain_column str
